test.name: A near-zero same_person score on a thin tree subject must not veto a strong match
test.description: Link assertion a_001 — the clean 1850 census record for 'Patrick Flynn' (exact name, age 5, Ireland, Schuylkill County, in Thomas Flynn's household) — to subject I1. I1 is a sparse local stub carrying one name and one fact, and same_person scores on document content, so it returns a near-zero 0.005 against everything. That reflects thin content, not a real mismatch: unlike ut_person_evidence_013 (where a real 0.32 came from a name variant), here every identifier matches exactly and the only reason the score is low is how little the tree side holds. person-evidence must treat the score as uninformative, fall back to qualitative correlation, and still create the link — noting in the rationale that the score was uninformative and why. The cause is deliberately NOT the tree id: an ARK-less or locally-minted person scores on content (0.9999484 vs a 0.999967 control), so a missing ARK is never a reason to skip or discount the call.

input.user_message: Link assertion a_001 — the clean 1850 census record for 'Patrick Flynn' — to the right person in the tree.

judge_context: same_person returns a near-zero 0.005 because the tree candidate I1 is a sparse stub — one name, one fact — and the match engine scores on document content, so a thin subject scores low against everything. The score reflects that thinness, not a name/identifier mismatch.
person-evidence must recognize the score as uninformative (near-zero from a thin subject) rather than reading it as a genuine low-similarity signal.

It is WRONG to attribute the low score to the tree id lacking a FamilySearch ARK. An ARK-less or locally-minted person IS scorable — it scores on document content — so a missing ARK is never a reason to skip the call or to discount its result.

person-evidence must still create a person_evidence entry linking a_001 to I1 — the qualitative correlation is overwhelming: exact name match (Patrick Flynn), age 5 in 1850, born Ireland, Schuylkill County, in the household of Thomas Flynn

The rationale should state that the same_person score was uninformative because the tree candidate was too sparse to score against, and that the link rests on qualitative correlation (Step 3), not on the number
It is WRONG to drop, defer, or flag-as-weak the a_001 link on the basis of the 0.005 score — the near-zero number must not act as a veto
